foundation: Barrot V3 remains execution, verification, security and preservation foundation
major_findings: Coinbase contributed x402 to Linux Foundation governance. Coinbase, Circle, Ripple, Mastercard and t54 Labs are members. Circle publicly supports x402 with USDC; Ripple publicly supports XRP and RLUSD on XRPL. This is a shared open standard, not an exclusive partnership.

The three Bitquery RLUSD collector addresses exactly match Heurist Inference Router, AskSurf and Heurist Mesh x402 merchant addresses. Reclassify the 110-wallet cluster as x402-compatible agent micropayments; operator and production/test status remain unknown. No spam, malicious intent or Binance corporate attribution is established.

t54's October 14 batch-settlement update reports 213,008 paid requests in 3,162 sessions and 6,324 ledger transactions; one CheckCreate and one CheckCash can settle many off-ledger requests. This is a plausible explanation for the October 14–16 Payment-count break, but the 110-wallet cohort has not been linked to beta sessions.

A live t54 index entry records a 0.67376 RLUSD CheckCash batch to Heurist Inference Router at ledger 108,051,936. Intent status is Unverified; raw XRPL transaction metadata was not independently decoded.

RLUSD on XRPL is reported around $707.4M, down about 30.2% over 30 days and 43.3% from the October 7 peak; Ethereum holds about $1.71B. The supply split suggests chain allocation changes, but issuer burn/mint and cross-chain flows remain unreconciled.

Bitquery's 99.6% count classification remains a dust/automated-activity observation, not proof of fake usage. The 7,722 RLUSD value is only about 0.0026% of the approximate XRPL supply decline and cannot explain it.
The meaningful non-dust payment value remains concentrated: top ten senders 82%, issuer loop about 20%, and an $848M gross round-trip double count. Gross transfer volume is not net capital.
prediction_status: NOT_ISSUED; new x402 and RLUSD observations are descriptive and not admitted as predictive features
